title: Long-Term Clinical and Functional Outcomes and Cartilage Regeneration Following Arthroscopic Matrix-Associated Autologous Chondrocyte Implantation for Focal Cartilage Defects of the Knee
summary:
Background and Objective

In some patients, the articular cartilage of the knee is so severely damaged that spontaneous regeneration is not possible. One treatment option is autologous chondrocyte transplantation. Although this procedure has been used for several years, evidence regarding its long-term outcomes and the factors influencing treatment success remains limited.

Former patients will be invited to participate in a follow-up examination. The function of the knee joint and morphological cartilage repair will be assessed using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and compared with the results of previous examinations. The findings are intended to improve the assessment of long-term treatment outcomes and provide physicians with a more robust basis for selecting suitable patients and counseling them regarding the expected outcomes of treatment.

Research Question

How should the long-term clinical and morphological outcomes following arthroscopic matrix-associated autologous chondrocyte transplantation (MACT) of the knee be evaluated? Is there an association between MRI findings and clinical outcomes, and can these findings provide insights into patient selection and the long-term prognosis following arthroscopic MACT?

 Methods

Study participants will be identified through a review of existing hospital records. Only patients who underwent arthroscopic matrix-associated autologous chondrocyte transplantation (MACT) of the knee between January 2017 and May 2020 will be eligible for inclusion. A total of 25 potential participants have been identified as eligible for consideration.

Potential participants will be contacted in writing and informed about the objectives, procedures, and content of the study. Interested patients will receive written patient information and an informed consent form. Participation in the study will be entirely voluntary and will take place only after written informed consent has been obtained.

As part of the follow-up examination, MRI of the operated knee will be performed. In addition, two validated questionnaires, the Lysholm Score and the International Knee Documentation Committee (IKDC) Score, will be used to assess the function of both the operated and the contralateral knee.

interventions.name:
Patients meeting the inclusion criteria who underwent arthroscopic matrix-associated autologous chondrocyte transplantation (MACT) of the knee between January 2017 and May 2020 will be identified through a review of their medical records and invited to participate in the study in writing.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Arthroscopic matrix-associated autologous chondrocyte transplantation (MACT) of the knee performed at the study center between January 2017 and May 2020.

Age ≥ 18 years at the time of study participation.
Exclusion criteria:
Absence of previous postoperative MRI scans for comparison with the current MRI examination.

Contraindications to MRI.

Absence of written informed consent to participate in the study.
